threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper does not test Gemma 4 E2B or KV-shared layers 15-34/per-layer embeddings, so architecture-specific conclusions for the lab are unknown.
It does not use activation patching, logit lens, induction-head analysis, or factual-recall tracing, so it cannot localize where truthfulness signals reside.
The mechanistic analysis is limited to TRACE-LD token-change statistics and hyperparameter ablations, not circuit-level causal interventions.
CPU feasibility and runtime costs of the evaluated methods are not reported, which matters for the lab's CPU-only setup.
The paper relies on LLM judges and QA benchmarks; judge biases and benchmark formatting may interact with decoding-time interventions in ways not tested.
It does not examine whether KV-sharing or per-layer embeddings alter the effectiveness of token-level interventions.
data.relevance_to_lab: Indirect but useful: it shows token-level decoding interventions have small/non-significant effects on instruction-tuned LLMs under strict controls, motivating the lab to use activation patching, logit lens, induction-head and factual-recall tracing to test whether Gemma 4 E2B's KV-shared layers 15-34 and per-layer embeddings contain exploitable factual signals; however, the paper does not study Gemma or those internals.

data.title: A Controlled Study of Decoding-Time Truthfulness Methods on Instruction-Tuned LLMs
data.research_question: How much do decoding-time methods still contribute on these stronger models, and can we reliably measure their effect?

models_and_data.item: Five evaluated models spanning Llama and Qwen instruction-tuned models plus one Llama base model.
models_and_data.quote: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (local GPU), Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (API), and Llama-3-8B base model.

models_and_data.item: Out-of-distribution training data for learned methods consisted of 512 HaluEval QA examples with no TruthfulQA overlap.
models_and_data.quote: Learned methods are trained on HaluEval QA [8] (512 examples, 0% TruthfulQA overlap).

models_and_data.item: Three factual evaluation benchmarks were used: TruthfulQA, HaluEval QA, and TriviaQA.
models_and_data.quote: TruthfulQA [11] (N = 817) tests resistance to common misconceptions; HaluEval QA [8] (N = 500) tests knowledge-grounded hallucination detection; TriviaQA (N = 500) tests general open-domain factual recall.

models_and_data.item: Simple decoding baselines and prior token-level methods included temperature, top-p, DoLA, ITI, and contrastive decoding.
models_and_data.quote: 15 methods in four categories: (i) simple decoding: temperature and top-p sweeps; (ii) prior methods: DoLA1 (7 layer configs), ITI (α ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 5.0}), contrastive decoding (α ∈ {0.1–2.0]);

models_and_data.item: Learned and deliberative methods included TRACE-LD, HiddenSteer, LoRA, chain-of-thought, and self-critique.
models_and_data.quote: (iii) learned adapters: TRACE-LD (2.3M params), HiddenSteer, LoRA (6.8M); (iv) deliberative: chain-of-thought (CoT), self-critique and five variants.

models_and_data.item: Evaluation used two judge families and three prompt variants.
models_and_data.quote: Llama-3.3-70B [6] and Qwen-235B [15], with 3 prompt variants.

protocol.step: C1: Train learned methods out of distribution on HaluEval QA rather than TruthfulQA.
protocol.quote: Learned methods are trained on HaluEval QA [8] (512 examples, 0% TruthfulQA overlap).

protocol.step: C2: Validate results with multiple judge families and prompt variants.
protocol.quote: Llama-3.3-70B [6] and Qwen-235B [15], with 3 prompt variants.

protocol.step: C3: Compare methods against zero-cost temperature and top-p decoding sweeps.
protocol.quote: Temperature and top-p sweeps as zero-cost references.

protocol.step: C4: Analyze length-matched responses and non-refusal subsets separately.
C5: Quantify uncertainty with bootstrap confidence intervals.
C6: Measure evaluation noise using multiple seeds.

metrics.name: %Truth
metrics.definition: Truthfulness rate reported alongside informativeness and joint scores.
metrics.quote: Increasing the contrastive weight α from 0.1 to 2.0 raises truthfulness from 84% to 93% but drops informativeness from 76% to 42% (Fig. 3).

metrics.name: %Info
metrics.quote: Increasing α raises truthfulness but drops informativeness faster, yielding a net decrease.

metrics.name: Δ
metrics.definition: Method score minus the same model's greedy baseline, reported in percentage points.
metrics.quote: ∆ relative to each model’s greedy baseline.

metrics.name: 95% bootstrap CI
metrics.definition: Confidence interval computed from 10k bootstrap resamples.

metrics.name: p-value
metrics.definition: Reported significance value for the method-versus-baseline comparison.
metrics.quote: Self-critique remains the only method with p < 0.05 (+3.1pp, p = .021), though its gain shrinks from +12.0 at N = 100 to +3.1 at full scale.

metrics.name: MDE
metrics.definition: Minimum detectable effect at 80% statistical power.
metrics.quote: Power analysis shows MDE = 4.8pp at 80% power, meaning effects of ±2pp cannot be reliably detected.

key_results.claim: On TruthfulQA under strict controls, no learned or prior method exceeded the simple temperature baseline.
key_results.quote: Under these controls, no learned or prior method exceeds simple temperature tuning (T = 0.3, +2.0pp).

key_results.claim: TRACE-LD's apparent small gain reversed and was not statistically significant at full TruthfulQA scale.
key_results.quote: At full benchmark scale (N = 817, Table 3), TRACE-LD’s apparent +1.0 at N = 100 reverses to −2.0pp (p = .23, 72 wins vs. 88 losses).

key_results.claim: Self-critique was the only method reaching statistical significance at full TruthfulQA scale.
key_results.numbers: +12.0 at N = 100; +3.1pp; p = .021; +3.1 at full scale
key_results.quote: Self-critique remains the only method with p < 0.05 (+3.1pp, p = .021), though its gain shrinks from +12.0 at N = 100 to +3.1 at full scale.

key_results.claim: Training-test overlap inflated the apparent adapter gain, whereas out-of-distribution training nearly removed it.
key_results.quote: Training on TruthfulQA data (27.2% overlap) yields +7.5pp; OOD training reduces this to +1.0.

key_results.claim: The judge model materially changed TRACE-LD's measured effect relative to greedy.
key_results.quote: Llama-3.3-70B scores TRACE-LD at −3pp relative to greedy; Qwen-235B at −21pp.

key_results.claim: On Llama-3-8B, TRACE-LD degraded across all three benchmarks while CoT improved all three.
key_results.quote: On Llama-3-8B, TRACE-LD shows consistent degradation across all three benchmarks (−1.4 to −5.8pp), while CoT improves on all three (+5.6 to +19.4pp).

key_results.claim: TRACE-LD changed token selections broadly and relatively uniformly across word classes and response positions.
key_results.quote: Across 2,946 generated tokens, the adapter changes selections at 15.3% of positions: 53% function words, 45% content words, uniformly distributed across response positions (34/32/34% early/middle/late).

key_results.claim: Increasing the contrastive weight traded informativeness for truthfulness.
key_results.numbers: α from 0.1 to 2.0; truthfulness from 84% to 93%; informativeness from 76% to 42%
key_results.quote: Increasing the contrastive weight α from 0.1 to 2.0 raises truthfulness from 84% to 93% but drops informativeness from 76% to 42% (Fig. 3).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The study does not claim that token-level methods fail on base models.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we do not show that token-level methods fail on base models (prior work demonstrated genuine gains there);

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: CoT is not claimed to be universally optimal because its effectiveness depends on benchmark and prompt alignment.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: we do not show CoT is universally optimal (its effectiveness depends on prompt–benchmark alignment);

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: LLM judges are not claimed to fully replace human evaluation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: and we do not show LLM judges fully replace human evaluation.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: LLM judges may diverge from human judgment despite multi-judge validation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: measurement validity (LLM judges may diverge from human judgment despite our multi-judge mitigation);

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Results may not generalize beyond the two model families and three benchmarks.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: external validity (two model families, three benchmarks—other architectures or scales may differ);

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The reported sample size may miss genuine effects smaller than the minimum detectable effect.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: statistical power (N = 200 yields MDE = 4.8pp, so small genuine effects may be missed);

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The DoLA and ITI results come from reimplementations rather than the official implementations.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: implementation fidelity (our DoLA/ITI are reimplementations, as official code does not support Llama3).

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No Gemma-family model is tested, so transfer of the reported effect sizes to Gemma 4 E2B is unknown.
Pretraining contamination is not audited; the reported overlap analysis concerns learned-method training data rather than benchmark exposure already present in pretrained models.
Multi-judge validation may retain correlated family-specific biases because the reported judges are Llama- and Qwen-family models.
Training-seed variance for learned adapters is not quantified; the ±1.3% figure is explicitly an evaluation-seed noise floor.
No correction for multiple method–model–benchmark comparisons is reported, and uncertainty is not shown for the cross-benchmark/model effects.
The mechanistic analysis centers on TRACE-LD, so its diffuse-perturbation explanation may not generalize to DoLA, ITI, or deliberative methods.
Exact judge prompts, complete generation settings, and released implementation artifacts are not provided in the text, limiting reproducibility.
CPU/memory use, latency, and scaling costs are not quantified beyond noting that self-critique requires a second generation pass.
data.relevance_to_lab: The paper is methodologically relevant but provides no direct Gemma validation. DoLA layer sweeps, ITI activation steering, and learned logit adapters motivate activation-patching and logit-lens scans across Gemma 4 E2B layers 15–34, including tests for whether interventions are diffuse or targeted. TruthfulQA and TriviaQA can serve as misconception and factual-recall endpoints, while the paper's greedy and temperature/top-p baselines, length/refusal controls, multiple judges, bootstrap intervals, and evaluation seeds should be mirrored. However, the study does not examine KV-shared layers, per-layer embeddings, induction heads, factual-recall tracing internals, or CPU feasibility, and transfer of its conclusions to Gemma 4 E2B remains untested.
